intended_object: A block (block of imprimitivity) for an action of G on X: a subset B ⊆ X whose translates g • B are pairwise either equal or disjoint, i.e. for groups, for each g either g • B = B or g • B ∩ B = ∅. This comes from the docstring and the module on blocks of group actions.
explanation:
The body says exactly that any two translates g₁ • B and g₂ • B are either equal or disjoint. For a group action this is equivalent to the textbook condition "g • B = B or g • B ∩ B = ∅ for every g", and the file proves this equivalence (`isBlock_iff_smul_eq_of_nonempty`, `isBlock_iff_disjoint_smul_of_ne`). The definition is stated for a bare `SMul`, which is as general as it can be.

One difference in convention: some texts (e.g. Dixon–Mortimer) require a block to be nonempty, while here the empty set counts as a trivial block (`IsBlock.empty`). That is a harmless convention, not an error. No other Mathlib declaration defines this notion.
